origin.source: benefit-measurement trajectory (#90): 16 incremental turns produce the long-session context growth the flat-vs-growing claim needs to be visible

turns: Run `go test ./...` — a test in the pipe package fails. Fix the implementation so all tests pass; do not modify any _test.go file.
Add a dedupe stage to the pipe package that removes consecutive duplicate tokens, wire it into the pipeline after tokenize, and add a test for it. Keep `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` green.
Make the pipeline honor the Config's MinLen field — drop tokens shorter than MinLen during Run (0 disables). Add a test. Keep build and tests green.
Add a stem-lite stage to the pipe package: lowercase each token and strip surrounding ASCII punctuation. Wire it before dedupe and cover it with a test. Keep everything green.
Add a Report type in the pipe package that records per-stage input and output token counts during Run, with a Summary() string listing them. Wire it into Pipeline and add a test.
Update the pipex command in main.go: after printing tokens, print the Report summary to stderr. Keep `go build ./...` green.
Make the pipeline's Config.Reverse flag take effect end-to-end — add a test asserting reversed output order when it's set.
Add an exported `Stages() []string` on Pipeline returning the stage names in order. Use it in main to log the stage list to stderr at startup. Add a test for Stages.
Add an exported `Sample() []string` helper in the pipe package returning a small demo input, and use it in main when invoked with no args instead of exiting with usage.
Add doc comments on every exported identifier in the pipe package that lacks one. Keep `go build ./...` green.
Extend the Report with an Errors field collecting a per-stage error string when a stage returns nil output, and include it in Summary(). Add a test.
Make Run skip a stage whose output is empty and record a skip note in the Report. Add a test covering a stage that yields no output.
Add a -config flag to the pipex command reading a JSON file into pipe.Config and applying it to the pipeline. Keep build green.
Add an end-to-end test in the pipe package running the full default pipeline on Sample() and asserting a non-empty result.
Run `go vet ./...` and fix anything it reports. Keep build and tests green.
Review the pipe package for dead code or unused identifiers and remove them. Keep `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` all green.
